subject: Customer request: temporary reserved lane + autoscale exception for Black Friday pilot
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@spruce-ai.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary reserved lane + autoscale exception for Black Friday pilot

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Spruce is excited to run a live pilot over Black Friday weekend. We have a short but very high-peak traffic window: we expect a 6-8x token throughput spike for ~36 hours.

Can Redwood provide a temporary reserved lane (GPU slice) for our pilot and a one-time autoscaling policy exception so our burst traffic doesn't trigger the standard throttles? We can sign an MOU and commit to pilot credits. Attached is our capacity plan (spruce_capacity_plan.xlsx).

High-level ask:
- Reserved lane: L4 pool, 4x slots for 36 hours starting 2027-11-26 00:00 UTC
- Autoscale exception: allow sustained burst above 200% for the window
- SLA: best-effort fallback to smaller model variants if capacity goes below threshold

Please advise what info you need (we can share traffic curves and expected QPS).

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Growth
Spruce Analytics

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary reserved lane + autoscale exception for Black Friday pilot

Forwarding Olivia's request — short ask from Spruce for a temporary reserved lane + autoscale exception for Black Friday pilot.

Quick summary:
- Window: 2027-11-26 00:00 UTC for ~36 hours
- Pool/model: prefers L4 (family) and 4 slots; willing to accept quantized variant if needed
- Wants autoscale exception to allow >200% sustained burst
- Will sign MOU and provide traffic curves (attached)

Action items: can infra/ops tell me:
1) Is a temporary carveout for that window feasible without impacting committed customers?
2) What approval path is needed for an autoscale policy exception?
3) If we can’t meet full ask, proposal for alternatives (e.g., scheduled warm-up, model variant fallback, cost estimate).

Marcus / Laura — can you take point on feasibility and ask ops for rough cost/impact? Dev — if we need a policy exemption, what telemetry/guardrails would you require?

Thanks — I want to get back to them this week with options.

—Neha
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary reserved lane + autoscale exception for Black Friday pilot

Couple quick notes from capacity planning sync:

- Feasibility: We can carve out 4 L4 slots for a 36-hour window, but it will require prebooking and a short maintenance window to pin the allocation (we'd need to finalize scheduling by 2027-10-31).
- Impact: Unless we place the carveout on low-utilization hosts in us-west, there's a ~12% risk to burst headroom for other uncommitted customers during that weekend. We should avoid overlapping with other major pilots.
- Autoscale exception: Ops can temporarily relax the throttle, but we must attach strict guardrails:
  * Time-bounded exception linked to the reserved lane window
  * Token burn alerting + automatic rollback if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds
  * Cap on total spend for the customer (pre-authorized credit)

Estimate: additional infra cost for the 36-hour window ~USD 18k-25k depending on pre-warm strategy; warm-up (prefetch/cache priming) reduces tail risk but costs more upfront.

Next steps: Laura, can you confirm availability of a low-util host pool? Dev, please list the telemetry and the runtime switches needed to implement the rollback guardrails. I'll start a tentative hold in the scheduling calendar.

-marcus
Senior Product Manager, Capacity

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary reserved lane + autoscale exception for Black Friday pilot

Dev notes (telemetry & runtime controls needed):

1) Telemetry
- Per-request token counters with 60s granularity (for burst detection)
- Tail latency p50/p95/p99 + 5xx error rate per deployment
- KV cache hit-rate for warm-up assessment

2) Runtime switches / guardrails
- Time-windowed policy flag that disables throttles for the customerID during the window
- Auto-rollback trigger: if p95 latency > 2.5x baseline OR 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5 consecutive mins -> rollback to default throttles and switch to model fallback
- Model fallback path: automatically route to compatible quantized model variant when rollback triggers
- Spend cap enforcement integrated with billing (stop serving when pre-authorized credit consumed)

3) Operational runbook items
- Pre-warm steps: run synthetic traffic for 2 hours before the window to populate KV caches
- On-call escalation: Page ops lead if rollback triggers

I can prototype the policy flag and rollback hooks; depends on a short config rollout (1 week), and we need Ops to enable the scheduling hold.

- Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@spruce-ai.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary reserved lane + autoscale exception for Black Friday pilot

Hi Olivia — thanks for the ask and the capacity plan. Short update and options:

1) Full reserve + autoscale exception (preferred)
- We can provision a temporary reserved lane: 4 L4 slots for 2027-11-26 00:00 UTC for ~36 hours.
- Ops will enable a time-windowed autoscale exception with the guardrails Dev listed. Estimated infra cost: ~$20k for the window.
- Requirements from Spruce: signed MOU, pre-authorized credit for the spend cap, and a 2-hour pre-warm window.

2) Reduced-risk alternative
- If Spruce prefers lower ops risk, we can provide 2 slots + scheduled warm-up + automatic model fallback (lower throughput but cheaper).

Please confirm which option you want and upload the signed MOU (I attached the MOU draft we discussed for edits). If you pick option 1, we'll put the tentative scheduling hold and start the config rollout for the policy flag.

Thanks — aim to finalize by 2027-10-01 to meet scheduling cutoffs.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- spruce_mou_draft.pdf (MOU template / terms)
